_comment: Craft. What makes documentation correct anywhere. No owner's decisions belong here.
_comment_contract: One definition generates the outline, prompts the author, and gates the result, so what is asked for and what is accepted cannot drift (see CONTEXT.md, Section Contract).

section_prompts.what: What this is, and explicitly what it is not. Name the boundary a reader could get wrong.
section_prompts.status: Where it stands today, dated. What is done, what is not. Never aspirational.
section_prompts.quickstart: Numbered steps, one action each, the exact copyable command. Every step says where it runs and what output proves it worked.
section_prompts.licen: Which licence covers this code, and where third-party notices live.
section_prompts.deploy: How it reaches a real environment, and every way that differs from the quickstart.
section_prompts.config: Every setting a reader must change: what it does, its default, and which file it lives in.
section_prompts.install: How a consumer installs this, the exact command, and which versions are supported.
section_prompts.api: The public surface. Link to the source; never restate signatures that will rot.
section_prompts.consumer: Who depends on this, so a breaking change has a known blast radius.
section_prompts.build: How to build and preview locally, and what the build produces.
section_prompts.content: The content model — what a non-developer edits, and where.
section_prompts.commands: Every command and what it does. This is the public surface of a CLI; link to the source rather than restating behaviour.

_comment_canon_profiles: The vendored checker resolves profiles/ beside itself, so a repo's CI copy needs them vendored too — without them P is {} and it dies in argparse before doing any work. The owner filename is named explicitly because there is one owner; a second would need this keyed off the remote.
_comment_canon_executable: Canon whose mode is part of the artifact. git records the bit (100755 vs 100644), so a hook written without it is inert in every clone.
_comment_org_inheritable: Files GitHub serves org-wide from a public .github repo, so a repo without its own is covered. CODEOWNERS, workflows and hooks are NOT inheritable and stay per-repo. Verified against GitHub's documentation 2026-08-08. NOTE: presence is read from the local .github clone, so a default sitting on an unmerged branch counts here while GitHub is not yet serving it. That is deliberate — the check stays offline — but it means these findings close on merge, not on commit.
_comment_canon_org: The only canon publishable to the world-readable org repo. CODEOWNERS names a person; the hook and the workflow describe our gate; and GitHub inherits none of the three regardless.
_comment_leak: Universal: anything that discloses infrastructure or identity on a public repo.
internal_patterns: unchecked hardening item — publishes what is not yet defended
_comment_policy: Null means the engine has no opinion. An owner's profile supplies one.
_comment_declared: Archetype is inferred from stack markers. Where no marker can tell (a CLI looks like a library), a profile declares it outright.
